place.source_title: Western Elevator Company, 507 North Appleton Street

brief: Crib-built wood grain elevator of 1901 (altered in the 1920s, demolished after 1989) sheathed in corrugated/pressed metal siding: a tall gabled bin block topped by a smaller gabled headhouse cupola, with a lower hip-roofed office and warehouse wing in front carrying a painted 'WESTERN ELEVATOR CO.' wall sign and a feed-brand sign, a shed-roofed truck canopy at the side, and a small cupola vent. It stood on an open gravel lot at a signalised street corner beside the railway, amid power poles.

facade.notes: the Western Elevator Co. (Appleton WI, 1901), HAER c.1989: a metal-clad wooden crib elevator -- a tall gabled bin block with a small gabled cupola (headhouse) on top, a lower hip-roofed office/scale house with a painted sign in front; on a gravel lot by the tracks at a signalled crossing, a commercial strip beyond

why.note: before concrete, elevators were cribbed planks sheathed in metal against fire
